name: Crude Oil (Niger Delta)
summary: Nigeria's dominant mineral resource — Africa's largest crude producer, concentrated in the Niger Delta.
description: Nigeria is Africa's largest crude-oil producer and a leading OPEC member. Reserves are concentrated in the Niger Delta basin, offshore deepwater, and shallows of the Gulf of Guinea. The Bonny Light and Forcados 40° blends are internationally traded benchmarks, and most crude is exported from Bonny, Forcados, Escravos, and Qua Iboe terminals. The industry has driven federal revenue since the 1970s while creating extensive environmental remediation, security, and political-economy challenges in the delta.
reserveNote: ~37 billion barrels proven (pre-2024 revisions, varying by source)
productionNote: ~1.5–2.3 million bpd (excluding shut-ins and crude theft); deepwater share growing
type: Light sweet crude oil (Bonny Light, Forcados, Qua Iboe, Escravos)
economy: Dominant share of federal export earnings and government revenue; dominates JV/PSC fiscal terms.
climate: Equatorial mangrove delta, shallow offshore, and deepwater blocks.
products: Gasoline / Premium Motor Spirit (PMS)
Diesel / Automotive Gas Oil (AGO)
Jet fuel / Aviation Turbine Kerosene (ATK)
Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) – cooking & power
Naphtha – petrochemical & gasoline blending feedstock
Kerosene – domestic lighting & cooking (DPK)
Fuel oil – marine, power generation, industrial boilers
Asphalt / bitumen – road paving & waterproofing
Lubricants & base oils – engine oils & greases
Petrochemical feedstock – ethylene, propylene, benzene
Plastics, synthetic fibres, synthetic rubber
Fertiliser (carbon black, sulphur byproducts)

name: Natural Gas (LNG & Associated)
summary: Africa's largest proven gas reserves; LNG exports via Bonny NLNG and growing domestic gas & NIPCo networks.
description: Nigeria holds Africa's largest proven natural-gas reserves, historically seen as associated gas flared from oil production. The Nigeria LNG (NLNG) plant at Bonny now ranks among the world's top LNG exporters, while the Escravos Gas-to-Liquids (EGTL), Obiafu-Obrikom gas gathering, Oben-Geregu pipeline, and the Ajaokuta-Kaduna-Kano (AKK) pipeline build a domestic gas grid for power, industry, and petrochemicals.
reserveNote: ~200+ trillion standard cubic feet proven (Tcf) — largest in Africa
productionNote: NLNG ~22 Mtpa (6 trains); domestic gas expanding via AKK pipeline & DS Phases
type: Associated & non-associated gas; LNG, LPG, CNG, GTL products
economy: LNG exports, domestic power/gas-to-plant, fertiliser, new petrochemical hubs.
climate: Delta swamps + shallow & deepwater blocks, northward gas grid.
products: Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG) – ocean-borne export cargo
Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) – transport & power
Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG / propane-butane) – domestic cooking
Electricity generation – open & combined-cycle gas turbines (the bulk of Nigeria's grid)
Fertiliser – urea, ammonia, nitrogenous blends
Methanol & methanol-to-olefins (MTO) petrochemical feedstock
Hydrogen & blue hydrogen – steel, ammonia, refineries
Gas-to-Liquids (GTL) diesel & naphtha (Escravos GTL)
Pipeline gas – cement, steel, glass, ceramics, food processing
Carbon black, acetic acid, formaldehyde, and downstream chemical intermediates

name: Coal (Enugu / Middle Belt)
summary: Historic Enugu sub-bituminous coalfields — Nigeria's first mineral export, now targeting power & cement.
description: Coal was Nigeria's first systematic solid-mineral industry, with the Enugu (Udi hills) fields powering port railways and export trade from Port Harcourt by the 1920s–50s. Modern efforts focus on sub-bituminous coal for captive power, cement blending, and proposed mine-mouth power stations (Kogi, Benue, Enugu, and Nasarawa).
reserveNote: ~2.4 billion tonnes indicated coal / lignite estimates
productionNote: Historic 300,000 tpa peak; small artisanal + rehabilitation projects since
economy: Coal to power, cement additives, domestic energy in coal belts.
climate: Guinea savanna–forest transition belt, Udi and Mambilla foothills.
products: Electricity generation – captive & mine-mouth coal-fired power plants
Cement manufacturing – blended with petroleum coke for kiln heat
Domestic heating briquettes – household & small-scale industry
Synthetic liquid fuels (CTL – coal-to-liquids) under study
Steel / smelting heat source – metallurgical coal for coke ovens
Industrial process heat – food, tobacco, textiles, brick kilns
Activated carbon – water purification & gold recovery
Coal-bed methane (CBM) – gas production from coal seams

name: Tin & Columbite (Jos Plateau)
summary: World-famous Jos Plateau alluvial tin and columbite deposits — a 20th-century mining legacy.
description: Tin and columbite (niobium-tantalum ore) were mined on the Jos Plateau from 1904 through the 1970s, driven by dredging of alluvial gravels. This created the landscape of mine ponds, reclaimed farmlands, and gullies that still shape the plateau. Remnant artisanal workings continue, and Nigeria is now exploring rare-metal pegmatites downstream of old leases.
reserveNote: Pegmatites with tin-tantalum-niobium still in-situ; reserve estimates vary
productionNote: Peak 1960s production made Nigeria a leading tin supplier; artisanal only today
type: Cassiterite tin, columbite (niobium), tantalite & lithium-cesium-tantalum pegmatites
economy: Heritage mining; current artisanal tin + rare metals exploration for batteries market.
climate: Highland Jos Plateau climate; cooler, rainfall influenced by orography.
landmarks: Jos Museum of Traditional Nigerian Architecture + mining exhibits
products: Tin metal (Sn) – solders for electronics assembly
Tinplate – food & beverage cans, aerosol containers
Tin alloys – bronze, bearing metals, pewter, fusible alloys
Niobium (columbite) – high-strength low-alloy (HSLA) steel for pipelines & structural
Niobium superalloys – jet engines, gas turbines, rocket nozzles
Tantalum (from columbite-tantalite ores) – electrolytic capacitors for phones & EVs
Lithium byproducts (from Jos pegmatites) – Li-ion battery precursor salts
Tin chemicals – PVC heat stabilisers, plating, catalysts, glass polishing

name: Iron Ore (Itakpe, Agbaja & Koton-Karfe)
summary: Itakpe iron-ore deposit supplies the Ajaokuta Steel Complex and the National Iron Ore Mining Company (NIOMCO).
description: Nigeria's principal iron ore deposits are the Itakpe hematite-magnetite ore (Kogi) and the Agbaja oolitic iron formation (Kogi/Enugu). NIOMCO at Itakpe ships beneficiated ore via rail to Ajaokuta and Delta Steel (Aladja), supporting Nigeria's long-delayed domestic steel programme. Recent interest includes direct-reduction iron for the Dangote-led Obajana/Ajaokuta revival efforts.
reserveNote: Itakpe proven + Agbaja indicated >2 billion tonnes of iron-formation
productionNote: NIOMCO: ~1-2 Mtpa beneficiated pellets/ore for Ajaokuta & Aladja
type: Itakpe magnetite-hematite, Agbaja oolitic iron, NSIA-backed Itakpe pellet upgrade
economy: Steel industry feedstock, Ajaokuta & Aladja steel mills supply chain.
climate: Guinea savanna on the Kogi plateau; proximity to Niger confluence.
products: Pig iron – blast-furnace intermediate for steelmaking
Steel rebars – concrete reinforcement (construction sector)
Structural steel – beams, angles, plates, sections (I, H, C)
Steel sheets & coils – roofing, automobiles, appliances, tinplate base
Beneficiated iron-ore pellets – feedstock for direct-reduction and blast furnaces
Direct Reduced Iron (DRI / sponge iron) – EAF steelmaking feed
Wire rods & drawn wire – nails, welding electrodes, mesh, fencing
Cast iron & ductile iron – pipes, manhole covers, engine blocks, cookware

name: Gold (Northwest & Southwest Belts)
summary: Emerging artisanal-to-industrial gold province across Zamfara, Kebbi, Kaduna, Osun and Niger.
description: Nigeria is increasingly recognised as a gold-bearing nation. Primary activity is artisanal and small-scale gold mining (ASGM) across a northwest Zamfara–Kebbi–Kaduna belt, plus the Ife-Ilesha schist belt in Osun/Ekiti. Formal large-scale mines are now under development, with the Presidential Artisanal Gold Mining Initiative (PAGMI) seeking to formalise production and reduce security and child-labour risks.
reserveNote: Millions of ounces indicated; world-class deposits targeted by juniors
productionNote: Several tonnes per year (mostly informal; PAGMI formalisation ongoing)
type: Lode & alluvial gold, Birimian-like schist belts of Nigeria
economy: ASGM livelihoods, formalisation via PAGMI, new junior miners & royalties.
climate: Sudan savanna northwest & Yoruba southwest, both with gold-bearing schists.
products: Jewellery & artisanal goldsmithing – the largest end-use in Nigeria
Investment gold – bullion bars, coins, Central Bank reserves
Industrial electroplating – corrosion-resistant coatings on electronics contacts
Electronics connectors & bonding wires – integrated circuits, PCBs, SIM cards
Dental alloys – crowns, bridges, inlays, prosthetic dentistry
Aerospace & defence – gold-coated reflectors, infrared shielding, radar
Catalysts – gold catalysts for vinyl acetate monomer (VAM) & pollution control
Decorative gilding – architectural leaf, textiles, traditional regalia

name: Limestone (Cement Belts)
summary: Extensive Maastrichtian limestone formations backing the Obajana, Sokoto, Calabar, and Mfamosing cement plants.
description: Nigeria's cement industry relies on thick Maastrichtian limestone sequences: (1) the Sokoto embayment (Sokoto cement plant), (2) the Nkalagu/Mfamosing belt east of the Niger (Dangote Obajana, Calabar cement, Lafarge Ashaka/Ugwuaji), and (3) smaller Ewekoro/Sagamu deposits north of Lagos. These deposits underpin Africa's largest cement producer (Dangote Cement) and the wider construction sector.
reserveNote: Tens of billions of tonnes — enough for 500+ years at current production
productionNote: Nigeria ~70+ Mtpa cement; Dangote Obajana alone >16 Mtpa
type: Maastrichtian limestone (Nkalagu, Mfamosing, Kalambaina, Ewekoro, Ashaka, Gombe)
economy: Cement manufacturing (Dangote, Lafarge-Holcim, BUA, Cement Co. of Northern Nigeria).
climate: Sudan-savanna in the north, tropical forest–savanna transitions in the southeast.
highlights: Backbone of Dangote African cement empire
products: Portland cement (OPC) – the dominant use (Obajana, Dangote, BUA, Ashaka, etc.)
Ready-mix concrete & precast concrete products
Construction & road aggregate – crushed limestone for base courses & chippings
Agricultural lime / ground calcium carbonate (GCC) – soil pH correction
Sodium carbonate (soda ash) & calcium chloride – detergents, glass, de-icers
Precipitated calcium carbonate (PCC) – paint, paper coating, plastics filler
Flux material – iron & steelmaking blast furnaces and smelting
Glass manufacturing – soda-lime glass for bottles, windows, tableware
Filler in rubber, pharmaceuticals (calcium supplements), toothpaste, cosmetics

name: Bitumen & Tar Sands (Dahomey Basin, Ondo)
summary: Onshore heavy-oil / tar-sand belt in Ondo/Edo – one of Africa's largest bitumen reserves.
description: Nigeria's eastern Dahomey basin holds extensive bitumen and tar-sand deposits, predominantly in Ondo and adjacent Edo/Ogun. The deposit is often ranked second to Canada's Athabasca region among global bitumen occurrences. Nigeria has long planned to produce synthetic crude, road asphalt, and diluent blends; pilot programmes and licence rounds remain active.
productionNote: Pilot-scale / asphalt only; major SAGD/dilbit projects planned
type: Tar sand / heavy oil / bitumen (Dahomey basin Agbabu, Ode-Aye belts)
economy: Asphalt for highways, proposed synthetic crude (upgraders), road contractors.
highlights: One of world's largest bitumen belts
products: Synthetic crude oil – upgrade tar sands via extraction & hydroprocessing
Paving-grade asphalt – highway & road surfacing (AC, SMA, HMA)
Bitumen emulsions – slurry seal, microsurfacing, tack coats, cold mix for rural roads
Waterproofing membranes & coatings – building roofs, basements, tunnels
Diluent for heavy crude pipeline transport (Orimulsion-style blends under study)
Roofing shingles, roofing felts, built-up roof (BUR) systems
Industrial binders – briquettes, carbon electrodes, pipe joint compounds
Asphalt for airport runways, port pavements, racetracks, parking areas

name: Lead-Zinc (Lower Benue Trough)
summary: Mississippi-Valley style lead-zinc mineralisation across Benue, Taraba, Nasarawa, Plateau belts.
description: Nigeria hosts a well-defined lead-zinc-silver mineral belt in the Albian–Turonian carbonates of the Lower Benue Trough and on the Jos Plateau margins. Deposits at Abakaliki (Ebonyi), Barikin Ladi and environs (Plateau), and in the Ibi-Muri belt (Taraba) have seen decades of artisanal mining, with modern ESG-focused juniors seeking to bring polymetallic (Pb, Zn, Ag, Cd, Cu) production online.
reserveNote: Millions of tonnes indicated Pb-Zn with Ag, Cd byproducts
productionNote: Artisanal Pb-Zn dominant; several formal-scale feasibility projects
type: Carbonate-hosted MVT Pb-Zn + vein Ag-Cd polymetallic ores
economy: Zinc galvanising, lead acid batteries, silver credits, growing junior mining.
climate: Benue trough Guinea savanna; Jos Plateau highlands.
products: Lead-acid batteries – automotive SLI, motive power (forklifts), stationary UPS backup
Galvanised steel – zinc coating on rebars, roofing sheets, pipes (corrosion protection)
Brass & bronze alloys – plumbing valves, fittings, bearings, decorative hardware
Zinc die-castings – automotive components, door handles, electrical housings
Silver bullion byproduct – from lead-silver smelting (Pb-Ag ores)
Cadmium plating & battery byproducts – historically, now restricted but still relevant
Zinc oxide (ZnO) – tyres (vulcanising activator), pharmaceuticals, sunscreen, ceramics
Zinc chemicals – dry-cell batteries, fertilisers (Zn micronutrient), pigments

name: Lithium & Rare Metals (Central / Nassarawa-Kogi-OGP)
summary: Subeconomic-to-economic lithium pegmatites in Nasarawa, Kogi, Kwara & Oyo — a fast-growing battery-minerals belt.
description: Nigeria's pegmatite fields carry spodumene, lepidolite, and rubidium-bearing micas alongside tin and tantalum in a corridor through Nasarawa, Kogi, Kwara, Oyo, Ogun, and Ekiti. Demand from lithium-ion battery markets has made the country a new frontier: artisanal concentrate exports have begun alongside MoUs with Chinese and Western juniors for larger EPC projects.
reserveNote: Early-stage; numerous pegmatites supporting small-scale & proposed large-scale
productionNote: Artisanal spodumene/lepidolite concentrate exports; JV DMS plants planned
economy: Battery mineral aspirant; MoUs for domestic lithium hydroxide refining.
climate: Guinea savanna with upland pegmatite belts.
products: Lithium-ion battery cells – EVs, residential storage, telecom backup, grid-scale
Lithium hydroxide & lithium carbonate – cathode precursor salts (NMC, LFP, LCO)
Tantalum electrolytic capacitors – consumer electronics, 5G base stations, automotive
Niobium HSLA steel – oil & gas pipelines, structural, automotive high-strength steel
Rubidium & caesium specialty electronics – atomic clocks, GPS, photoelectric cells
Spodumene / lepidolite concentrates – feedstock for lithium refineries
Rare-earth magnets (NdFeB) – EV motors, wind turbines, hard-disk drives, speakers
Cerium / lanthanum catalysts – fluid catalytic cracking (FCC), automotive three-way catalysts

name: Marble & Solid Minerals (Kwara, Bauchi, Ondo)
summary: Crystalline marble belts supporting cement, decoration, and agricultural-lime industries.
description: Nigeria hosts commercial marble deposits in the Kabba-Koton-Karfe corridor (Kogi/Kwara), Jakusko (Yobe), and crystalline limestones at Ore (Ondo) and Buram (Bauchi/Gombe). These supply dimension-stone cladding, cement raw mix, and agricultural lime.
reserveNote: Billions of tonnes of marble-grade carbonate rocks
type: Dolomitic & calcitic marbles; crystalline limestones (Sokoto, Jakusko, Ore)
economy: Cement mix, dimension stone, agricultural lime, sodium carbonate projects.
products: Dimension stone – polished floor tiles, wall cladding, stairs, vanity tops, countertops
Cement raw-mix feed – high-calcium marble ground and blended with limestone
Agricultural lime / soil conditioner – calcium carbonate for acid soils
Ground calcium carbonate (GCC) – paint & coatings extender, paper filler, plastics
Sculpture, monuments, headstones, and decorative architectural elements
Soda ash (sodium carbonate) projects – glass and detergent feedstock
Whiting / filler for rubber, adhesives, sealants, and cosmetic powders
Table tops, window sills, facade panels, and mosaic / tile murals

name: Salt & Potash (Lake Chad Basin, Nasarawa & Lagoon Evaporation)
summary: Lake Chad solar salt pans, inland brines in Nasarawa/Benue, and Lagos lagoon-evaporation salt.
description: Salt production in Nigeria comes from three sources: (1) solar evaporation in the Lake Chad–Komadougu Yobe basin, (2) inland salt springs and brine pans in Nasarawa (Keana), Benue, and Plateau, and (3) coastal lagoon-evaporation schemes around Lagos/Ogun. Domestic production falls short of demand, driving imports and Dangote-led industrial salt refineries (e.g., Lekki) tied to chlor-alkali and food-grade salt.
reserveNote: Huge saline lake + lagoon-evap potential; brine reserves Nasarawa
productionNote: Artisanal solar salt + Dangote industrial refineries (Lekki, Calabar)
type: Rock salt, sea/lagoon evaporation, brine springs; potash from lake-basin brines
economy: Edible salt, chlor-alkali / caustic soda, leather tanning, fertiliser.
climate: Sahel lake-basin in the north; equatorial lagoons in the south.
products: Edible / table salt – iodised cooking salt, food-grade sodium chloride
Chlor-alkali industry – caustic soda (NaOH) + chlorine (Cl₂) electrolysis
Polyvinyl chloride (PVC) feedstock – chlorine + ethylene from refineries
Leather tanning – sodium chloride for pickling hides before chrome tannage
Potash fertilisers (NPK blends) – potassium for cash crops (cocoa, oil palm, cereals)
Soap & detergent manufacturing – soda ash feedstock and salt-based surfactants
Water softening & de-icing salts – industrial boilers, highway maintenance
Food preservation, curing brines, fermentation, and dyeing textiles
